claim: The three processes of Davidson and Sternberg (selective encoding, combination, comparison) are defined and linked to giftedness, but the full text was not read and no founding numbers were retrieved; the account has no direct LLM test. Gap search: only the ERIC abstract is accessible, so founding numbers remain missing.
agent_test: Prompt ablation: add an explicit step (what to keep, how to join, what to recall) to the framing stage; compare with plain CoT at equal tokens on insight-style items (BRAINTEASER, NazoNazo).

claim: Insight and non-insight problems are not cleanly separable by solving process: Aha ratings differ by problem class, but accuracy is similar and 12-13% of non-insight problems show a warmth jump.
agent_test: Do not branch the agent on problem class; test a uniform schema versus a class-routed one on mixed item sets.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Aha experience predicts correctness (Aha solutions more often right), yet false insights exist: 37% of wrong magic-trick solutions got above-average Aha, and primed lures produced false Aha at d about 1.5. Grimmer et al. 2022 (not 'Laukkonen 2022') Exp1 N=150: lure false-insight rate 0.37 vs 0.07-0.09, d 1.49-1.73; Exp2 smaller (d about 1.0-1.1).
schema_part: G# (do not trust felt certainty or 'wait' cues)
agent_test: Log the model's own aha/wait markers and its confidence; measure accuracy given marker at equal tokens.

claim: Warmth ratings are flat then jump on insight problems but climb steadily on non-insight problems (classic result), though one magic-trick study found no warmth difference between insight and non-insight solvers.
agent_test: Use token-level confidence trajectories as an analogue and compare shapes across item types.

claim: Concurrent verbalisation hurts insight problem solving and helps non-insight: 57% vs 13% on the deer problem, 30% vs 80% on cryptarithmetic (N=120). Single lab. Earlier studies conflict (Fleck & Weisberg, Gilhooly 2010: no effect; Ball 2015 mixed), so the human effect is not settled. In LLMs, CoT harms 3 of 6 verbal-overshadowing-style tasks (GPT-4o implicit learning 87.5 to 64.4) but this was not tested on insight items.
schema_part: G# (forced verbalisation may harm some items)
agent_test: Compare silent short answers versus long CoT on lateral-thinking items at matched tokens; look for a double dissociation by item type.

claim: Pupil data link incubation-period arousal to later solving (solvers n=11, non-solvers n=29, controls n=42); tiny solver group, one lab.
agent_test: Analogue only: insert an unrelated task between attempts and test whether resampling afterwards helps at equal tokens.

claim: Insight problem solving relates to working memory and reasoning ability, favouring a business-as-usual view over a special process; evidence here is titles and a review framing only. Salmon-Mordekovich & Leikin 2023 (N=115): analogical thinking predicts insight, divergent thinking about 2%, secondary tasks do not harm insight; verdict 'not that special but not quite as usual'. Chuderski 2018 numbers (51.8%, 84.6%) remain unverified.
agent_test: None directly; background.

claim: Dual-process (Type 1 / Type 2) framing is defended as autonomous versus working-memory-dependent processing; whether it explains insight is unresolved.
agent_test: Background only.

claim: Early GPT-3 models mimic human intuitive errors on the CRT (80% intuitive for davinci-003, 5% correct), whereas ChatGPT-3.5 and GPT-4 are 59% and 96% correct. Verified against the arXiv full text.
agent_test: Re-run CRT-type items on the agent's base model with rewritten items to rule out memorisation.

claim: Chain of thought acts as System 2 for weaker models (davinci-003 correct 5% to 28%, intuitive 80% to 29%), but blocking it barely hurts ChatGPT-3.5/4, so strong models have internalised it.
schema_part: S# (budgeted deliberation; skip when the model is strong)
agent_test: Run no-CoT versus CoT versus scaffold at equal tokens on a strong model; expect little gain on CRT, test on lateral items.

claim: Reasoning prompts help davinci-003 but not humans; worked examples help both (humans +0.14 correct), so a note that examples did not help humans would be wrong.
agent_test: Low priority.

claim: Insight-like lateral puzzles remain hard for LLMs: BRAINTEASER ChatGPT 53% (sentence) and 63% (word) versus human 92% and random 25%; rewording robustness is low; tuned or prompted systems reach 100% on a held-out subset in SemEval-2024 (contamination possible). Prompt effects on GPT-3.5 sentence puzzles: direct 72.5-75.0 beat CoT 60.0-72.5 (n=120); GPT-4 zero-shot 76.7 to 90.0 with explanatory few-shot CoT; word puzzles 53.5 to 84.4 with five examples, suggesting format learning.
agent_test: Evaluate scaffold versus plain on BRAINTEASER original plus semantic and context variants using group-based accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: On Japanese riddles needing representational change, non-reasoning models score 7.6%, reasoning models 17.6%, humans 52.9% (OR 2.29 for reasoning). Verified against the paper; one research group. Authors admit items are public and propose a rotating private set; few-shot with reasoning demonstrations helped all 4 tested models, significant in 2.
agent_test: Replicate a subset with the scaffold; track gap closure at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs often write the correct answer in their thought log yet reject it (verification failures 5.23% to 39.34% of wrong answers by model), like a failed feeling of rightness.
agent_test: Add a candidate-retention rule (no dropping a candidate without a stated reason); count verification failures with and without it.

claim: Spontaneous mid-trace Aha/wait shifts are rare (6.31%) and mostly do not help (accuracy 2.57% shifted versus 16.44% non-shifted); a cue forced at high token entropy lifted MATH-500 by 8.41 points but crosswords by 0.45. Liu et al. independently find aha keywords already in base models without reliable accuracy gain. Domain split: math shifts hurt at all temperatures (GPT-4o 0.658 vs 0.338); crosswords shifts looked better but not significant (AME 0.033, p=0.26). No riddle or lateral tasks tested.
schema_part: G# (no trust in self-correction cues), S# (externally triggered reconsideration)
agent_test: Compare entropy-gated forced reconsideration versus spontaneous reflection versus none at equal tokens on math and lateral items.

claim: Selective encoding done by an LLM (System 2 Attention, rewriting the context first) raises factuality 62.8% to 80.3% and distractor math 51.7% to 61.3%. Verified. One paper.
agent_test: Add a context-rewrite step before solving on distractor-laden items; count the token cost.

claim: Dual-process agent architectures (fast small model plus slow planner) beat single-process agents on ScienceWorld (84.7 vs 45.3 Reflexion, 36.4 ReAct, 33.8 SayCan); verified, but not matched on compute and not about insight.
agent_test: Route easy items to a cheap pass and hard ones to the slow schema at equal total tokens.

claim: LLM insight performance depends on how searchable the item is: parity or better on verbal insight items (ChatGPT at modal human score; GPT-4o beats humans on rebus) but clear deficits on representational-change tasks.
agent_test: Stratify an item set by lexical searchability and test the scaffold on the low-searchability stratum.

claim: No study found tests selective encoding, combination and comparison as an LLM scaffold directly. Gap search again found none; nearest are d04 (step-structured CoT worse than direct on GPT-3.5) and d05 (examples that explain why wrong options fail help GPT-4). Neither is equal-token.
agent_test: Gap; design the three-step ablation ourselves.

claim: A prescribed step-by-step structure is not automatically better than direct answering on lateral puzzles: GPT-3.5 sentence puzzles direct 72.5-75.0 vs Specified-Internal-CoT 60.0-62.5 (n=120); GPT-4 direct 95.0 vs simple CoT 97.5.
schema_part: S# (keep framing step short; compare against direct)
agent_test: Run the three-step framing prompt against direct answers on BRAINTEASER and a fresh set at equal tokens.

claim: High BRAINTEASER scores are partly format learning or tuning: word puzzles 53.5 to 84.4 with five examples (GPT-3.5), and the top SemEval sentence entry reached 98.3 overall. No uncontaminated lateral set exists; NazoNazo authors propose a rotating private set.
agent_test: Write new lateral items after the model cutoff and score with group-based accuracy.

claim: Chain of thought can lower accuracy on tasks where verbal thinking hurts humans (3 of 6 tested; GPT-4o implicit learning 87.5 to 64.4, faces 64.0 to 51.2, exceptions 2.9 to 12.5 rounds), and longer reasoning can lower accuracy on distractor tasks.
agent_test: Compare no-CoT and CoT on pattern-recognition and insight items and set a skip rule.

claim: Spontaneous aha/wait markers are not a reliable accuracy signal across domains: they hurt in math at all temperatures and are not significant in crosswords; a forced reconsideration cue gains +8.41 pp on math but +0.45 on crosswords. No data on riddles.
agent_test: Run the forced cue on a lateral item set.

claim: Outside replication of Macchi 2025 verbalisation and Grimmer 2022 false insight was not found. Verbalisation results conflict across labs; false-insight replication is within the original lab (Exp2) with a smaller effect plus one broadly consistent outside study (Ammalainen & Moroshkina 2021).
agent_test: None; treat both as single-lab effects.
